Subject: Re: High error rates / latency spike impacting inference for billing service

Marissa / Hannah —

Quick technical summary from infra triage (on-call):
- We see a sustained increase in KV cache churn for rwd/llama-2-13b-q8 on the shared hosted tier serving NovaGrid’s route. Cache hit-rate dropped from ~78% to ~34% starting ~06:35.
- The model instance pool hit mem pressure leading to repeated GC/evictions; p999 latency rose as a result. Error budget burned is mostly QoS timeouts and occasional OOMs.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:00 PT):
- Temporarily drained heavy affinity requests and routed NovaGrid traffic to a warmed standby pool (reduces throughput by ~20% but stabilizes latency).
- Increased GPU pool headroom for the route (scaled +2 nodes, hot-redeploy).
- Enabled aggressive prefix caching and bumped batch size down to lower tail latency for short sequences.

Next steps (please review for exec):
- Short-term (0–2 hrs): keep standby routing + scale, monitor p50/p95/p999, and throttle large-batch callers.
- Mid-term (2–24 hrs): propose dedicated pool for NovaGrid (reserved) and quantization/ops tuning to reduce memory churn.
- Post-incident: full RCA and model kernel telemetry review.

I’ve attached the raw latency samples we pulled and the prod arch diagram to this thread for reference.

Connor O’Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachments referenced:
- novagrid_latency_sample.log (extracted logs, 48KB)
- prod_arch_diagram.pdf (diagram, 120KB)

Subject: Status update — NovaGrid routing & mitigation steps (incident IR-1182)

Sam —

Thanks again for the quick signal this morning and for your patience. Summary of current state and next steps: 

What we observed: p999 latency and 5xx errors beginning ~06:35 PT tied to KV cache churn and memory pressure on the shared model pool serving your route.

What we did (completed):
- Diverted your traffic to a warmed standby pool to stabilize tail latency (09:00 PT).
- Scaled the pool by +2 GPU nodes and hot-redeployed (09:15 PT).
- Tuned batching and enabled more aggressive prefix caching (09:30 PT).

Immediate impact: error rate reduced from ~18% -> 3% and p999 latency trending down (still monitoring). We expect p999 to be within SLA by ~18:00 PT if current trends continue.

Proposed next steps (customer-facing):
- Short-term: continue standby routing and monitoring for 24 hrs.
- Mid-term: provision a dedicated pool for NovaGrid (24–48 hrs) — this reduces cross-tenant memory churn and gives predictable p99/p999.
- Post-incident: joint RCA + a performance tuning run (within 5 business days).

Credits & remediation: we propose a 25% service credit for the affected window if we fail to meet SLA by EOD PT. We’re prepared to expedite the dedicated pool for you and will share MAP and costs within 1 business day.

Next immediate touch: 12:00 PT bridge with execs (Jonas & Hannah joining) for a brief status and trust-repair. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/IR123456

Apologies again — we take this seriously and want to restore full confidence. If you agree to the 12:00 bridge, I’ll send calendar and dial-in.

Regards,
